It is often used as a name for a place or a person that offers shelter or security, such as a mosque or a leader. The name is also frequently used in Islamic literature and poetry, where it is used metaphorically to represent the idea of seeking refuge in Allah or the Prophet Muhammad (PBUH).

It can be seen as a reflection of the fundamental belief in the oneness of God and the need to turn to Him for guidance, strength, and solace. The name also reflects the concept of tawakkul, or complete trust and reliance on Allah, which is a central aspect of Islamic spirituality. Seeking protection through righteous deeds, such as prayer, charitable giving, and good actions, is also an important part of this spiritual understanding. Ultimately, the name Ghayasaa serves as a reminder of the enduring power of faith and the strength that can be found in turning to Allah for guidance and refuge.
